headline: Madhavpura replay: the warning a disclosure screen could not honestly give
dek: Madhavpura Mercantile Co-operative Bank is classified as fraud-masked. Its record does not establish an early warning from either the PCA-style or funding lens; it establishes a boundary between reported filings, market prices, and model output.

review_notes: Reframed null and unscoreable fields as observability limits rather than negative stress findings.
Separated filing-period disclosures, market-price data, and model or tier authority.
Retained fraud-masked, eligibility, stale-data, construction-PIT, and market-admission disclosures.
Removed placeholder-style status labels and retained the underlying eligibility and timing disclosures in plain language.
Separated filing-period observations, unavailable market-price evidence, and model or tier authority throughout.
Preserved fraud-masked status, unscoreable funding status, construction-PIT limits, stale-data exclusions, and market publication restrictions.

corrections.summary: Three co-operative bank failures in the India crisis record are dated at their onset, the first RBI directions restricting depositors, instead of the later licence cancellation. The India figures were regenerated, and Failure Radar tier publication is paused pending re-validation.
corrections.note: **Correction, 3 November 2026.** LiquiLens now dates three co-operative bank failures in its India crisis record at their onset, the first RBI directions restricting depositors, instead of the later licence cancellation: Madhavpura Mercantile Co-operative Bank on 13 March 2001 (previously 4 June 2012), CKP Co-operative Bank on 2 May 2014 (previously 30 April 2020) and Rupee Co-operative Bank on 22 February 2013 (previously 22 September 2022). Sources: RBI press releases of [7 June 2012](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=26606), [5 May 2014](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=31124) and [25 February 2013](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=28200). Each bank's only scored filing fell after its onset, so all three are now unscored for insufficient data rather than flagged. This article originally gave 2012-06-04, the day Madhavpura Mercantile Co-operative Bank's licence cancellation took effect, as its default date; the text below now gives 2001-03-13. The India figures cited below were regenerated: the share of non-fraud failures flagged moved from 88.9% to 86.7% (13 of 15), and the median lead from 21.5 to 23 months. Failure Radar tiers are now paused pending re-validation. Board states and validation statistics below are as served on the publication date, and the text is otherwise as published.
